issues.legal_issue: A substantially delayed challenge to a completed land acquisition may be denied as equitable writ relief where the claimants’ conduct is inconsistent with continuing to challenge the acquisition.
material_facts: The acquisition notification was issued in 1971, the award was made and possession was taken in 1976, and the writ petition challenging the acquisition was filed in 1992.
The claimants later sought execution of the award, and the execution proceedings led to a civil revision in which the acquiring authority deposited the compensation amount.
Two of the owners claimed compensation before the acquiring authority, and another owner authorised one of them to act and receive compensation on his behalf.
The land had been reserved for public purposes in the development plan since 1952.
The claimants did not disclose the execution application in their amended writ petition.
issues.conclusion: The High Court should not have granted relief. The writ petition was dismissed because the delay and the claimants’ conduct defeated their entitlement to equitable relief.
issues.legal_principle: Relief under Article 226 of the Constitution is discretionary and equitable; delay defeats equity, and equity favours a vigilant rather than an indolent litigant. Although no fixed limitation period governs the writ, the ordinary period for bringing a civil proceeding is a relevant guide. The Court considered N.L. Abhyankar v. Union of India, [1995] 1 MHLJ 503, and relied on Municipal Corporation of Greater Bombay v. Industrial Development Investment Co. Pvt. Ltd., [1996] 11 SCC 501. It distinguished Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd. v. Dolly Das, [1999] 4 SCC 450, which concerned a different legal context and different facts.

rule.if: acquisition_writ_challenge and substantial_delay and acquisition_completed and (claimant_pursued_award_execution or claimant_claimed_compensation)

predicates.acquisition_writ_challenge: The claimant brought a writ proceeding challenging a land acquisition.
predicates.substantial_delay: The claimant waited a substantial period after the acquisition steps before bringing the challenge.
predicates.acquisition_completed: An award had been made and possession of the acquired land had been taken.
predicates.claimant_pursued_award_execution: The claimant sought to have the acquisition award executed.
predicates.claimant_claimed_compensation: The claimant asserted a claim for compensation for the acquired land.
predicates.equitable_writ_relief_denied: The claimant is denied equitable relief in the writ proceeding.

issues.definition: When a claimant substantially delays a writ challenge to a completed acquisition and also pursues execution of the award or claims compensation, equitable writ relief is denied.

issues.legal_issue: A writ challenge to an acquisition notice or proceedings cannot be brought after the acquisition award has been made and possession has been taken.
material_facts: The award for the acquired land was made in 1976 and possession was taken that year.
The claimants filed their writ petition in 1992 and sought to quash the acquisition notification and obtain possession of the land.
issues.conclusion: The acquisition challenge could not succeed after the award had been made and possession had been taken.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on C. Padma v. Deputy Secretary to the Government of Tamil Nadu, [1997] 2 SCC 627, which held that after the acquisition proceedings have become final and possession has been taken, the former owners have no right to challenge the notification. It also relied on Municipal Corporation of Greater Bombay v. Industrial Development Investment Co. Pvt. Ltd., [1996] 11 SCC 501, which states that courts should be loath to quash acquisition notifications after the award and possession, while considering the relevant factors in exercising their discretion under Article 226 of the Constitution.

predicates.acquisition_notice_writ_challenge: The claimant brought a writ challenge to an acquisition notice or proceedings.
predicates.award_made: An award for the acquired land had been made.
predicates.possession_taken: Possession of the acquired land had been taken.
predicates.post_award_acquisition_challenge_not_ent: A writ challenge to the acquisition notice or proceedings is not entertained after the award and taking of possession.

issues.definition: A writ challenge to an acquisition notice or proceedings is not entertained when an award has been made and possession has been taken.

issues.legal_issue: A plea of limitation or laches is not barred merely because it is raised during the hearing rather than in the first reply.
material_facts: The acquiring authority raised the plea of delay and laches during the hearing and had also included it in an affidavit filed before the hearing began.
The High Court treated the timing of the plea as a reason the acquiring authority could not raise it.
issues.conclusion: The High Court erred in treating the plea as barred by the time at which it was raised; the plea could be considered.
issues.legal_principle: A limitation issue is a mixed question of law and fact. Although the plea ought to be raised at the first available opportunity, that does not bar a party from raising it during the hearing; in this case it had also been raised in an affidavit before the hearing commenced.

predicates.writ_acquisition_case: The proceeding is a writ challenge concerning a land acquisition.
predicates.laches_raised_during_hearing: The respondent raised a plea of delay or laches during the hearing.
predicates.laches_stated_in_prehearing_affidavit: The respondent had stated the plea of delay or laches in an affidavit filed before the hearing began.
predicates.laches_plea_not_barred_by_timing: The plea of delay or laches is not barred merely because it was raised at that stage.

issues.definition: In an acquisition writ case, a plea of delay or laches raised during the hearing and stated in a pre-hearing affidavit is not barred by its timing.
